# Meridian Harbor Logistics - Data Governance and Records Retention Policy

Document ID: MHL-POL-014
Version: 4.2
Owner: Office of the Chief Data Officer
Classification: Internal - Approved for Staff Distribution

## 1. Purpose

This policy establishes how Meridian Harbor Logistics creates, classifies, stores,
protects, retains, and finally disposes of recorded information across every business
unit. It applies to structured records held in the freight management platform, to
semi-structured operational telemetry emitted by terminal equipment, and to
unstructured material such as correspondence, scanned bills of lading, and internal
reports. The policy exists so that a single, predictable rule set governs the life of a
record from the moment it is created until the moment it is irreversibly destroyed, and
so that no department invents its own private retention practice.

## 9. Roles and responsibilities

The Chief Data Officer owns this policy and the retention schedule. Data stewards,
appointed one per business unit, classify new record types, respond to audit findings,
and act as the first point of contact for retention questions. System owners are
accountable for ensuring that the systems they operate are registered with the records
engine and that disposal actually executes. Every employee is responsible for not
creating unmanaged copies.

## 10. Compliance and exceptions

## 10. Compliance and exceptions

Internal Audit tests this policy twice yearly against a sample of record types drawn
from each tier. Findings are tracked to closure in the enterprise issue register.
Exceptions are time-bound, require the written approval of the Chief Data Officer and
the relevant business unit director, and expire after twelve months unless renewed.
There is no such thing as a permanent exception to this policy.

Questions about the application of this policy are directed to the data steward of the
relevant business unit in the first instance, and to the Office of the Chief Data
Officer where the steward cannot resolve them.

## 3. Devices

Remote access is permitted only from a managed device. A managed device is enrolled in
the company endpoint management platform, carries full disk encryption, runs a supported
operating system version, has the endpoint detection agent installed and reporting, and
has received security updates within the last fourteen days. A device that falls out of
compliance loses access automatically and regains it when compliance is restored.

Personal devices may be used for electronic mail and calendar through the managed
container only. No other company system is reachable from a personal device. Printing
company material at home is not permitted; where a physical copy is genuinely required
it is produced at a company facility and handled under the clear desk standard.

## 4. Network access

## 5. Legal hold

A legal hold suspends deletion. When the General Counsel issues a hold, the records
engine marks the affected record set and the automated disposal routine skips it. A
record under hold is retained until the hold is lifted in writing, regardless of its
scheduled retention period. Staff who become aware of actual or threatened litigation,
a regulatory inquiry, or a customs investigation must notify Legal within one business
day and must not delete or alter potentially relevant material in the interim.

Holds are reviewed quarterly. A hold that has been open for more than eighteen months
without a documented reason is escalated to the Data Governance Council for a decision
to continue or release.

## 6. Disposal

These four figures - ten years, seven years, one hundred and eighty days, and thirty
days - constitute the complete retention schedule. No business unit may extend a
retention period by local decision. Where a longer period is genuinely required, the
request is submitted to the Office of the Chief Data Officer with a written statutory or
contractual basis, and if accepted it is published as an amendment to this section
rather than kept as an informal exception.

Retention periods are measured from the event date carried on the record, not from the
date the record was ingested into a given system. A record copied into a downstream
analytics store inherits the retention clock of its source; the copy does not start a
new clock. This is the single most frequently misunderstood provision of this policy and
it is the provision most often found violated during internal audit.

Meridian Harbor Logistics operates inland terminals and bonded warehousing in four
regions. Each region previously maintained separate archival conventions. The 4.0
revision of this policy consolidated those conventions; the present revision clarifies
the treatment of telemetry and model training corpora.

## 2. Scope

This policy binds all employees, contractors, secondees, and third-party processors who
handle company records in any medium. It covers primary systems of record, replicas,
backups, exports, analytics extracts, and any copy held on an endpoint device. A copy of
a record is a record. Staff may not create a parallel retention regime by moving data
into a personal drive, a spreadsheet, a messaging thread, or an unmanaged cloud bucket.

## 3. Roles

The **duty analyst** holds first-line responsibility around the clock and is the only
role permitted to declare an incident. The **incident manager** coordinates the response
once an incident is declared and is drawn from a rota of six trained staff. The
**technical lead** is appointed by the incident manager for each incident and directs
containment and recovery work. The **communications lead** owns all internal and
external messaging. The **executive sponsor** is the Chief Information Security Officer
or, in their absence, the Chief Operating Officer.

Named deputies exist for every role. No role may be left vacant during an active
incident; if the primary holder is unreachable for fifteen minutes, the deputy assumes
the role automatically and does not wait for a handover.

This plan describes how Meridian Harbor Logistics detects, triages, contains, and

incident irrespective of origin: external intrusion, malicious insider activity,

# Meridian Harbor Logistics - Vendor Integration and API Error Handling Standard

Document ID: MHL-STD-022
Version: 2.5
Owner: Platform Engineering
Classification: Internal - Approved for Staff and Approved Suppliers

## 1. Purpose

This standard defines how external parties integrate with the Meridian Harbor Logistics
freight platform, what guarantees the platform offers them, and how errors are
represented so that both sides can diagnose a failure without a telephone call. It is
written for supplier engineering teams as much as for internal ones, and an approved
supplier may be given this document in full.

## 2. Integration patterns

Three patterns are supported and no others are offered.

**Synchronous REST.** The caller issues an HTTPS request to the regional gateway and
receives a response within the published timeout. Used for lookups, bookings, and
status queries.

# Meridian Harbor Logistics - Business Continuity and Terminal Resilience Plan

Document ID: MHL-PLN-003
Version: 5.0
Owner: Operational Resilience
Classification: Internal - Approved for Staff Distribution

## 1. Purpose

This plan sets out how Meridian Harbor Logistics continues to serve its customers when a
disruptive event removes people, premises, systems, or suppliers from normal operation.
It covers the four inland terminals, the bonded warehousing estate, the shared service
centre, and the freight platform on which all of them depend.

Continuity planning is distinct from incident response. Incident response restores a
failed system. Continuity planning keeps the business operating while the system is
still failed. Both may run at once and they are coordinated through the operations
bridge.

## 2. Critical business services

## 4. Manual workarounds

Every critical service has a workaround that functions without the freight platform.
Gate processing falls back to paper movement notes issued from a numbered pad held in
the gate office, with reconciliation into the platform once it returns. Customs
declaration submission falls back to direct submission through the authority portal by
the customs team, at reduced volume. Dangerous goods authorisation falls back to the
duty supervisor working from the printed segregation tables, which are reissued
quarterly and held in the control room.

## 3. Recovery objectives

Recovery objectives are expressed as a maximum tolerable period of disruption and a
maximum tolerable data loss. Gate processing and container release must be restored
within two hours with no more than fifteen minutes of data loss. Customs declaration
submission must be restored within four hours with no more than one hour of data loss.
Dangerous goods handling authorisation must be restored within one hour with no data
loss, since the manual workaround for this service is intentionally conservative and
reduces throughput sharply. Reefer monitoring must be restored within thirty minutes
with no data loss. The remaining three services carry a twenty-four hour objective.

Error codes are grouped by first character. Codes beginning with A are authentication
and authorisation failures. Codes beginning with V are validation failures and indicate
that the request was understood but malformed. Codes beginning with R are resource
failures: a referenced booking, container, or consignment does not exist or is not
visible to the caller. Codes beginning with T are transient and the caller should retry
with backoff. Codes beginning with E are internal errors and the caller should not
retry the same request without contacting support.

The complete code catalogue is published in the developer portal and is versioned
alongside this standard. Codes are never reused and never redefined; a code that is
withdrawn is marked deprecated and continues to be documented.
